dataset: Oddshot validation: resolved non-sports election markets

source_endpoints.purpose: Public event and market metadata, outcome prices and CLOB token identifiers.
Public CLOB historical token prices; query includes market token, startTs/endTs and fidelity=1 minute.

markets.news_source: AP News, “Sen. Ed Markey, 80, wins Mass. Democratic primary over opponent who called for generational change”
markets.news_timestamp_basis: AP story timestamp as published by AP search metadata (04:05:06 UTC); story reports Markey secured the nomination. This is a publication-time proxy, not a separately logged AP Decision Desk call timestamp.
markets.resolution: YES (Ed Markey won the Democratic nomination)
markets.description: Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts. AP reported Markey won; market closed YES.

gamma_event_snapshot.title: Massachusetts Democratic Senate Primary Winner
gamma_event_snapshot.description:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Massachusetts.

If no 2026 Massachusetts Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Massachusetts Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

gamma_market_snapshot.question: Will Ed Markey be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Massachusetts?

caveats: CLOB prices-history returns sampled/traded history points, not a guaranteed quote for every wall-clock minute; returned timestamps are irregular despite fidelity=1.
The price queried is the YES outcome token for the named candidate. It is a last-trade/history series, not an executable midpoint or full order book.
News moment uses the AP publication timestamp as the best reproducible timestamp found; actual internal decision desk call/declaration may have preceded publication.

markets.news_source: AP News, “Former US Sen. John E. Sununu to face US Rep. Chris Pappas in New Hampshire Senate race”
markets.news_timestamp_basis: AP story timestamp (04:03:54 UTC) is the first located publication explicitly reporting Pappas as the Democratic nominee; publication time is a reproducible proxy, not a separately logged AP Decision Desk call timestamp.
markets.resolution: YES (Chris Pappas won the Democratic nomination)
markets.description: Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in New Hampshire. AP reported Chris Pappas won; market closed YES.
